title: Bend at the hips with a hinge, not a spine lean
summary: lean() rotates only the spine bones: a hunched curve. hinge(f, a) tips the pelvis forward by a and turns both thighs back by a (the legs stay put), then a little lean on top: a real bow at the hips.

versions.note: seed harvest of the shot-match scenes (L3)

doc.when: Diggers, pushers, people picking something up or looking into a hole.
doc.avoid: lean() alone for anything past ~.3 rad.
gotchas: Works on any skeleton with a pelvis and thigh bones.

problem.symptom: A 'bent over' figure looks hunched, with the hips upright.
problem.cause: Spine-only rotation curves the back; the reference bends at the hip joint.
problem.fix: hinge(f, a) first (pelvis forward, thighs back), then a small lean.
problem.detect: Side view: the pelvis stays vertical while the back curves.
